messages.content:
Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 42
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: South Eastern Asian
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Project Manager
  trauma_type: Life-threatening illness
  pcl5: 67

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Olfactory (Smell): Related smells, Cold Temperature: Cold, Visual (Needles/Medical): Medical equipment such as needles or drips
  Maladaptive Strategies: Memory Erasure: I try to erase the memory of the event, Thought Monitoring: constantly monitor own thoughts for signs of going crazy, Avoid Medical Cues: Hospitals/ Ambulances/ Physical Examinations
  Memory: Story Feels Unreal: The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me, Emotion Without Image: Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory, Partial Clarity: Some moments of the event are extremely clear while others are completely blank
  Negative Appraisals: Life Destroyed: My life has been destroyed by the trauma, Failed Role: I have failed in my most important role in life, Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened

Vignette:
Samantha, a 42-year-old South Eastern Asian woman and a Project Manager, has been grappling with the aftermath of a life-threatening illness that she endured two years ago. The traumatic event has left indelible marks on her psyche, manifesting in various symptoms that have significantly impacted her daily life. The incident began as a routine medical check-up but quickly escalated when Samantha was diagnosed with a severe and unexpected illness. The hospital environment, filled with the scent of antiseptics and cold temperatures, became synonymous with fear and vulnerability. During her treatment, she endured multiple invasive procedures involving needles and intravenous drips, each one reinforcing the feeling that her body had been invaded and damaged beyond repair. In the months following her discharge from the hospital, Samantha found herself constantly trying to erase the memory of the event. She would distract herself with work projects or household chores, attempting to push the traumatic experience out of her mind. However, this effort was often futile as she would be suddenly overwhelmed by the intense emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory accompanying it. This disconnect made her feel that the memory was too extreme to believe it had actually happened to her. Samantha's fear extended beyond just the memories; she became hyper-vigilant, constantly monitoring her own thoughts for signs of going crazy. The mere sight of medical equipment, hospitals, ambulances, or even the prospect of a physical examination would send her into a panic. She avoided any reminders of the traumatic event, including places that smelled like antiseptics and cold environments reminiscent of the hospital. This avoidance behavior had significant consequences in both her personal life and work. As a Project Manager, Samantha found herself struggling to attend mandatory health screenings at her workplace, leading to missed opportunities for promotions and increased stress from potential health concerns going undetected. Her husband noticed that she became increasingly distant and irritable, avoiding family gatherings where medical topics might come up in conversation. Samantha's negative appraisals of the trauma have been deeply internalized. She believes that her life has been destroyed by this event and that she has failed in her most important role—whether it be as a wife or a professional. The physical vulnerability she feels is a constant reminder of the permanent damage her body has endured, leading to a pervasive sense of fragility and fear. Despite these challenges, Samantha's symptoms had gradually worsened over time, reaching a point where she could no longer function effectively in her daily life. The culmination was when she found herself unable to attend an important work conference due to her intense fears about being near medical personnel or feeling cold temperatures, which ultimately led to significant professional consequences. It was this breakdown that finally prompted Samantha to seek help. She is most afraid of reliving the traumatic experience and losing control over her emotions and thoughts. However, she also hopes for a way to reconcile the fragmented memories and intense feelings so that she can regain a sense of normalcy in her life and fulfill her roles both personally and professionally.
